conclusions.question: Is a single-field TTL index {exp: 1} with expireAfterSeconds 5 accepted, and how does listIndexes report it?
conclusions.answer: Accepted; createIndexes replied {"raw": {"defaultShard": {"numIndexesBefore": 1, "numIndexesAfter": 2, "createdCollectionAutomatically": true, "ok": 1}}, "ok": 1}. listIndexes reports {"v": 2, "key": {"exp": 1}, "name": "exp_ttl", "expireAfterSeconds": 5, "storageEngine": {"enableOrderedIndex": true}}, identical to the open-source index document (expireAfterSeconds is an int32 5, storageEngine.enableOrderedIndex true).

conclusions.question: Is a second single-field TTL index on another field (exp2) of the same collection accepted?
conclusions.answer: Accepted; createIndexes replied {"raw": {"defaultShard": {"numIndexesBefore": 2, "numIndexesAfter": 3, "createdCollectionAutomatically": false, "ok": 1}}, "ok": 1} and listIndexes shows {"v": 2, "key": {"exp2": 1}, "name": "exp2_ttl", "expireAfterSeconds": 5, "storageEngine": {"enableOrderedIndex": true}}.

conclusions.question: Does the second TTL index expire documents through its own field?
conclusions.answer: Yes: exp2_past_date_60s (exp2 = Date 60 s in the past, no exp field) was deleted between ['2026-11-25T21:05:52.103+00:00', '2026-11-25T21:06:07.195+00:00'] (server clock), i.e. at the 2026-11-25T21:06:00.000+00:00 boundary, in the same 15 s window as past_date_60s and array_of_dates from the exp_ttl index, so both TTL indexes on the collection are purged on the same per-minute schedule.

conclusions.question: Is a compound TTL index accepted?
conclusions.answer: No: code 67 CannotCreateIndex, errmsg 'Error in specification { "expireAfterSeconds" : 5, "name" : "ab_ttl", "key" : { "a" : 1, "b" : 1 } }:TTL indexes work only on single fields, and compound indexes are incompatible with TTL functionality.', no errorLabels field in the reply; byte-for-byte the same errmsg as the open-source engine.

conclusions.question: Is a non-numeric expireAfterSeconds accepted (open-source parity check)?
conclusions.answer: No: code 67 CannotCreateIndex, errmsg 'Error in specification { "expireAfterSeconds" : "abc", "name" : "exp3_bad", "key" : { "exp3" : 1 } }:The \'expireAfterSeconds\' option for a TTL index must be a numeric value, but a different data type was provided: string.', no errorLabels; identical to the open-source engine.

conclusions.question: Which exp values expire?
conclusions.answer: Only BSON Date values: past_date_60s, array_of_dates ([past Date, Date +1 day]; one expired element is enough) and future_date_90s (after it passed exp + 5 s) were purged; string_value, number_value, missing_field, null_value (ISO string, int64 epoch milliseconds, missing field, null) were never purged in 300 s although a Date with the same instant would have been eligible for about 295 s.

conclusions.question: What is the TTL purge cadence on the managed service?
conclusions.answer: Once a minute at the top of the server-clock minute. In 300 s of 15 s polling there were 4 purge events, each inside the poll window that straddles a minute boundary (21:06:00, 21:07:00, 21:08:00, 21:09:00 UTC, windows at second 52.2 to 07.2); every one of the 4 boundaries that had eligible documents deleted all of them; nothing was deleted in any of the 15 poll windows that contain no minute boundary (0 with a deletion), although eligible documents were waiting in 12 of them; consecutive events were 45.0-75.0 s apart (one per minute). The 1 s fine probe put the 21:11:00 run between 21:10:59.579 and 21:11:00.678 server clock. No mid-minute deletion occurred: future_date_90s became eligible at about 21:06:42, was still present at the 21:06:52 poll and was gone only after the 21:07:00 boundary, so the release-note 'continuous for up to 60 seconds' behaviour did not delete newly eligible rows mid-minute on this idle collection (in the engine source that loop only continues while a run is still deleting rows).

conclusions.question: What is the lag between eligibility (exp + expireAfterSeconds) and deletion?
conclusions.answer: The time left until the next minute boundary, so 0 to just under 60 s on an idle cluster. Observed brackets after eligibility: 0.0 to 60.2 s; all 19 purged Date documents were deleted at the first boundary after eligibility, which means lags of 7.8-53.0 s for the phases tested (eligible at second 07: 52.8-53.0 s, eligible at second 22: 37.8 s, eligible at second 37: 22.8 s, eligible at second 42: 18.0 s, eligible at second 52: 7.8 s); the fine probe, eligible on insert at second 07, was gone [52.4, 53.5] s after insert. DECISIONS topic 10 open item 5 can be closed for this tier: 'expiry happens at the first minute boundary after expireAfterSeconds has elapsed; allow up to about 60 s'. Behaviour with many expired rows was not tested.

conclusions.question: Side observation: what clock information does the managed gateway expose for timing TTL tests?
conclusions.answer: hello.localTime is returned as BSON int64 epoch milliseconds ({"$numberLong": "1795640683762"}), not as a BSON Date as MongoDB documents it; server minus client offset was [0.006, 0.008] s by hello.localTime and 0.011 s by $$NOW, so the Mac and server clocks agreed to about 10 ms.

conclusions.question: Side observation: what shape is the createIndexes reply on the managed service?
conclusions.answer: mongos style: {"raw": {"defaultShard": {"numIndexesBefore": 1, "numIndexesAfter": 2, "createdCollectionAutomatically": true, "ok": 1}}, "ok": 1}; code that reads numIndexesAfter at the top level gets nothing. The open-source run recorded only the helper's return value, so the shapes were not compared.

amendments.was: Single-field TTL index exp_ttl accepted: ok=1, numIndexesBefore=None, numIndexesAfter=None, createdCollectionAutomatically=None.
amendments.now: Single-field TTL index exp_ttl accepted (ok=1); reply is per shard under raw: defaultShard: numIndexesBefore=1, numIndexesAfter=2, createdCollectionAutomatically=True.
amendments.why: first-version reading read numIndexesBefore/After at the top level; the managed reply nests them under raw.defaultShard

amendments.step: create second TTL index on exp2 (expireAfterSeconds 5)
amendments.was: Second single-field TTL index exp2_ttl on the same collection accepted: ok=1, numIndexesBefore=None, numIndexesAfter=None, createdCollectionAutomatically=None.
amendments.now: Second single-field TTL index exp2_ttl on the same collection accepted (ok=1); reply is per shard under raw: defaultShard: numIndexesBefore=2, numIndexesAfter=3, createdCollectionAutomatically=False.
amendments.why: first-version reading read numIndexesBefore/After at the top level; the managed reply nests them under raw.defaultShard
db.command() returns a naive UTC datetime; the first version called .timestamp() on it, which applied the Mac's local UTC-8 offset (28800 s)

caveats: Observed on one M30 single-shard cluster with HA disabled and an almost empty collection on 2026-11-25 at engine versions ['2.2-1', '2.3.0', '12.1-1']; cadence under load (many expired rows, the 60 s continuous-batch budget) was not tested.
15 s polling brackets each deletion to a 15 s window; the 1 s fine probe is a supplement to pin the run time.
Client timestamps were converted to the server clock with the measured hello.localTime offset; hello.localTime is returned as int64 epoch milliseconds.
